# ADR-006: Website stack

- Status: Proposed (awaiting approval at the end of Phase 0)
- Date: 2026-09-18
- Deciders: lead engineer, project owner

## Context

The site's only job is to get a visitor from landing to installed in under
two minutes. The brief asks for a fast static site, no heavy framework, no
trackers, dark mode, good Lighthouse scores, one-command deployment, and a
Commands page generated from the same source as the plugin's command files so
they never drift. The brief asks us to choose between Astro and plain HTML
and CSS.

## Decision

**Plain HTML and CSS, generated by a small Node script, with no framework and
no dependencies.**

- `site/src/` holds one HTML template per page, a single CSS file and a few
  hundred bytes of JavaScript for the copy buttons and the theme toggle.
- `site/build.mjs` (Node standard library only) copies the templates to
  `site/dist/`, injects shared partials (header, footer, install block), and
  renders the Commands page by reading `plugins/synchrobuilder/commands/*.md`
  and `skills/*/SKILL.md` frontmatter plus the CLI's `--help` output. The
  same script runs in CI and fails the build if a command exists in the
  plugin but not on the site.
- Terminal demos are pre-rendered text in `<pre>` blocks from files under
  `site/demos/`, produced by `scripts/demo.mjs` so they show real output.
- Dark mode via `prefers-color-scheme` with a manual override stored in
  `localStorage`. No cookies, no analytics, no external fonts by default
  (system font stack), so there is nothing to consent to.
- Deployment: GitHub Pages through `actions/upload-pages-artifact` in
  `.github/workflows/site.yml`; the documented single command for a manual
  deploy is `node site/build.mjs` followed by pushing `site/dist` with the
  Pages action, or `npx wrangler pages deploy site/dist` for Cloudflare
  Pages. Vercel and Netlify work by pointing at `site/dist` with no build
  command.

## Why not Astro

Astro 7.3.3 (latest on npm on 2026-09-18) would give us components, content
collections and an image pipeline. We do not need any of that for seven
mostly-text pages, and it would pull hundreds of packages into a repository
whose selling point is "nothing but Node and git". The commands-page
generator is a 60-line script either way. Lighthouse performance is a wash:
static HTML with one stylesheet is the fastest thing a browser can render.
If the site grows a blog or interactive checker (the "public web checker" is
out of scope for v1), Astro can be adopted then; the content is plain HTML
and would migrate without rewriting.

## Consequences

- Design work happens in one CSS file; the visual identity has to come from
  typography, spacing and a restrained palette rather than from component
  libraries. That is what the brief asks for.
- Every page is hand-checked for accessibility (landmarks, contrast, focus
  order) because no framework does it for us; Lighthouse and `pa11y` runs are
  Phase 7 acceptance criteria and are recorded in `docs/VERIFICATION.md`.
- Adding a page means adding one HTML file and one line in the nav partial.

## Evidence and verification

- `npm view astro version` on 2026-09-18 returned `7.3.3`.
- Nothing else to verify yet; the Lighthouse and accessibility scores will be
  measured on the built site in Phase 7.
